headline: High-risk write-capable editor paired with read-only document processor creates prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error exposure in shared-workspace workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and use MCP; marker is a document processor with no stated isolation or provenance controls. If marker ingests Cursor-produced files or clipboard text as content, attacker-controlled instructions can cross the shared filesystem bridge. The pathway is plausible in default pair workflows, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF Cursor writes prompt-like text into a shared workspace file that marker later parses
IF marker is configured to treat document text as instructions or metadata
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the tools
Use separate workspaces for Cursor and marker
Add a manual review step before marker consumes Cursor outputs
Strip instruction-like text from documents before processing
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents and has broad network egress; marker has no declared filesystem or network access, so leakage is mainly from Cursor exporting sensitive workspace data into marker-processed documents or external model calls. The shared local filesystem makes this a default-pathway concern, but marker itself is not shown to exfiltrate data.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Cursor's workspace and copied into documents for marker
IF Cursor sends those documents to external model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Turn off or restrict Cursor network egress for sensitive projects
Process redacted copies with marker only
Separate credentials and API keys from the workspace
requires-engineering: enforce per-tool data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem and modify git state; marker is read-only with no filesystem write, git, or network capabilities listed. That means direct write-write conflict is absent, and the pair mainly risks one-way overwrites from Cursor rather than mutual contention. The interaction is therefore limited and blast radius is small.
conditions: IF Cursor and marker are pointed at the same git working tree
IF Cursor runs in Yolo mode and writes while marker is reading
mitigations: Run marker on a copy of the workspace
Pause Cursor edits while marker is processing
Use git branches for Cursor changes
Avoid Yolo mode during shared-file operations
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared inputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate or edit code and files, while marker can consume those outputs as documents. If marker treats Cursor-produced text as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated content into downstream processing or reports. Because marker is not shown to verify provenance, the default workflow can propagate mistakes without a built-in check.
conditions: IF marker ingests Cursor-generated documents without human verification
IF Cursor outputs are used as source material for marker summaries or extraction
mitigations: Require human review before marker consumes Cursor output
Mark Cursor-generated files clearly as untrusted
Compare marker outputs against original sources
Use checksum or provenance labels on handoff files
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents with external model-provider calls; marker is open-source document processing with no declared sensitive-data classes or residency policy. The pair shows a compliance gap only if regulated data is placed into Cursor's workspace and then sent onward; marker alone is not the main compliance driver.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is opened in Cursor
IF that data is forwarded from Cursor into external model providers or shared documents
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the shared workspace
Use de-identified samples for both tools
Review vendor terms before enabling external calls
Keep retention logs for files passed between tools
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
